note: Files this archive deliberately revised after materializing the pinned deployment. Every entry explains one difference from the historical pin in package.json. An entry is a reviewed change record, never a way to silence unexplained drift: a file that differs from both its historical pin and this list stays DRIFT.

revisions.name: contract.json
revisions.reason: Declare the P32D2 basic admission point in a separate basic_admission block, keeping the scale series prefills and decodes arrays unchanged so the 24 scale cases keep their identity, and add a display name per model so a receipt or a case id does not have to be read as a version string. Declare evidence_points: prefill 128 with decode 2 and 16 for qwen25_1p5b, the two points that have independent three-repeat NCU references. This reverses the earlier exclusion, which named P128D2 as an example of a pair that must be refused: the accepted evidence and the declared matrix could not both be right, and the evidence is what a run must reproduce. scale_series and basic_admission keep their axes, so the 26 existing cases keep their identity.

revisions.name: matrix_workload.py
revisions.reason: Derive the case axes and the accepted (model, prefill, decode) triples from contract.json instead of a hard-coded tuple, so a declared point can actually be selected, and reject undeclared pairs such as P32D128 or P128D2. The accepted case now records its declared_matrix name. Derive the evidence_points block the same way as basic_admission, so declaring a point is what makes it selectable and an undeclared model in the block is refused.

revisions.name: sample_pipeline.py
revisions.reason: Call matrix_workload.add_arguments instead of repeating the choice tuples, and validate the (model, prefill, decode) triple in the parent process. The duplicated gate is what previously rejected a declared point before it reached host.py; per-axis choices alone cannot see a pair such as P32D128, which would otherwise fail only inside the host child.

revisions.name: run_job.py
revisions.reason: Accept seconds = 0 as no wall-clock deadline. The replay entry documents that it has no deadline, so the controller must be able to express that instead of capping every job at 86400 s. Positive values keep the 1..86400 bound and the receipt records wall_clock_deadline.

revisions.name: followthrough.py
revisions.reason: Accept --model-uncovered and forward it to expand_profiles.py, and record the coverage of the expansion in the stage finish receipt before the memgen stage is allowed to run.

revisions.name: profile_cache.py
revisions.reason: Same no-deadline fix for the cache stage, which killed the child at seconds + 60. --seconds is accepted and ignored.

revisions.name: expand_profiles.py
revisions.reason: Add --model-uncovered modeled, which completes a class with no admitted template as an explicit numeric_modeled object-volume profile (memgen-adapter/model_uncovered.py) instead of refusing its launches. The default stays refuse: a missing profile is still never a zero-traffic kernel. Modeled rows are counted separately (exact_launches, modeled_launches, modeled_fraction, modeled_by_cause), carry status PASS_MODELED_UNCOVERED_CLASS with model.target_addresses_hardware_observed false so the r4 original-allocation guard can still refuse them without a release re-pin, and the manifest now states fully_exact, exact_cross_layer_identity_claimed false and the HBServe-style not_claimed list.

revisions.name: run_memgen.py
revisions.reason: Carry the expansion coverage fields (modeled_completion, exact_launches, modeled_launches, modeled_fraction, modeled_by_cause, fully_exact) from the expanded manifest into the replay receipt, so a result that used modeled completion cannot be read as a fully exact stream.

claim_boundary: Producing a declared point is not an accuracy result and not an admission decision. validation/p32d2_branch_status.csv remains the authority for hardware-accuracy admission.
